replacement.title: Support the carrier after a give-and-go look
replacement.objective: Keep supporting when the first pass changes the puck carrier and the return lane is shaded.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). YOU have just passed to F2; D1 is on the direct return line between you. F1 is on the other side of the middle of the rink and may offer another option.
cues: D1 shades the old return line.
F1 is a visible alternate support player.

questions.prompt: What changed when the pass reached F2?

options.text: F2 became the puck carrier
YOU became the puck carrier again
D1 became a teammate

questions.explanation: The setup assigns the puck to F2, so your job is now support and scanning.

questions.prompt: Which two details should shape your next support spot?

options.text: F2's current puck position
D1's relationship to the old return line
Where the earlier pass started, without checking the new carrier

questions.explanation: F2 and D1 help you judge whether to change your support angle. Recheck the available space; a return pass is only one possible continuation.

questions.prompt: Arrange this post-pass support read.

options.text: Find F2 and the shaded line
Look for a new support angle with separation
Re-check F2, D1 and F1

questions.explanation: Read the carrier and coverage before changing your angle, then recheck. F1 may offer another option if a lane is available.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the side boards to offer a new angle to F2.
questions.explanation: The example adds width and moves the direct return line away from D1. Recheck the passing lane and F1; the new angle does not guarantee an available pass.

questions.prompt: F2 carries toward the middle instead of returning. What should YOU do?

options.text: Adjust support relative to F2 and call the available lane
Follow F2’s route without checking D1’s new lane
Hold the old return point without checking F2’s route

questions.explanation: Support follows the actual carrier. Update F2’s route and D1’s lane instead of chasing blindly or holding the old return point.

questions.prompt: What can your support accomplish when F2 keeps the puck?
questions.explanation: It can pull D1, offer a second lane, or protect F2's next option. Describe the named space and make the benefit conditional on D1's response.

replacement.objective: Offer a reset behind pressure while preserving a forward option.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). F1 controls the puck inside an attacking-zone faceoff circle. D1 is between F1 and YOU; D2 is farther toward the right net and across the middle. YOU can look for a reset closer to centre ice than F1.

D1 is between F1 and YOU.

questions.prompt: Where is the puck carrier in this freeze?

options.text: F1 inside the attacking-zone circle
YOU in the neutral zone
D2 nearer the right net

questions.explanation: F1 is the navy puck carrier inside the circle. YOU are a teammate; D1 and D2 are opponents.

questions.prompt: Which two features make a reset offer usable?

options.text: F1 can see and reach the offer
The offer stays separated from D1 and D2
The reset name matters more than the space around F1

questions.explanation: A reset is helpful because it is reachable and safer from pressure; if either cue changes, another route may be better.

questions.prompt: Arrange this conditional reset plan.

options.text: Read F1's pressure and the defenders
Move behind the pressure with separation
Re-check the reset and forward lanes

questions.explanation: The movement creates an option; the final scan decides whether F1 uses it, carries, or protects.

questions.prompt: Move YOU behind F1 and toward the middle to show a separated reset lane.
questions.explanation: This example is closer to centre ice than F1 and farther from D1. Keep checking D2 and the passing lane; another separated point may also work.

questions.prompt: D2 drops into the reset lane. What should F1 and YOU revisit?

options.text: Whether a new support angle or protected carry is available
The same backward pass as if D2 had not moved
A direct pass through D2

questions.explanation: If D2 closes the reset lane, YOU can look for a new angle while F1 checks space to carry or protect. Reassess before passing.

questions.prompt: What would you communicate while offering this reset?
questions.explanation: Call the pressure and offer the reset while its lane stays clear. If D2 closes it, communicate a new support angle or available carry space.

Approach under control

Knowing whether F2 remains reachable

questions.explanation: Keeping D1 on one side can buy time for F2 to become visible or draw coverage. The pass remains conditional on F2's lane and pressure.

Whether D1 can close from inside
